target.title: fix(llm-slug): use truncateUtf16Safe for LLM-prompt-facing session content truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LLM-prompt-facing text truncation uses raw UTF-16 `.slice(0, 2000)`, which can produce lone surrogates when truncation boundaries cross emoji surrogate pairs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace raw `slice` with the canonical `truncateUtf16Safe` helper:

`src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.ts` — `generateSlugViaLLM` truncates session content at 2000 chars for the LLM slug-generation prompt.

## User Impact

None for typical text. Session content that contains emoji at the truncation boundary may previously have produced malformed text in the LLM prompt, leading to invalid slug generation or provider errors.

## Evidence

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e "
import { truncateUtf16Safe } from '@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice'; 

const text = 'x'.repeat(1999) + '🚀' + 'yz'; 
console.log('BEFORE slice(0,2000): contains lone surrogate', /[\uD800-\uDFFF]/.test(text.slice(0, 2000))); 

const safe = truncateUtf16Safe(text, 2000); 
console.log('AFTER truncateUtf16Safe: contains lone surrogate', /[\uD800-\uDFFF]/.test(safe));"
```

```
BEFORE slice(0,2000): contains lone surrogate true
AFTER truncateUtf16Safe: contains lone surrogate false
```

- **Same pattern** as the 5 recently merged PRs (#102477, #102470, #102378, #102266, #102225) which fixed the same truncation issue across the codebase
- **Changes**: +2/-1 lines, imports existing `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`
